fieldMarks: All-black crow, 36-41 cm, slightly smaller than the American crow with slightly more pointed wingtips.
Identified with certainty only by voice: a nasal 'kwok' and a nasal two-noted 'ah-ah'.
behavior: Mostly a permanent resident; withdraws from some inland parts of its range in winter.
On the coast hunts salt marshes and tidal flats and scavenges on beaches; inland follows swamps and large river drainages.
Often nests in loose colonies of a few pairs.
Has expanded its range farther inland and north, notably on the Atlantic coastal plain and up the Mississippi Valley.
habitat: Tidewater, river valleys, swamps, woodland and farmland, usually nearer water than the American crow, especially beaches, marshes and estuaries.
range: Eastern and southeastern United States: Florida, the Southeast, Texas, the Mid-Atlantic and New England, extending up river valleys into the Plains and Great Lakes region.

lookalikes.name: American crow
lookalikes.howToTell: The American crow gives a familiar 'caw' rather than a nasal 'kwok' or 'ah-ah', though young American crows also make nasal calls in breeding season.
